findings.claim: The RMDC26 schedule "pauses F146 seven times per 70.7-day season for ~6 h, at fixed season phases". Training on the "exact schedule" "does not transfer better" and "matches the random-gap arm at every budget on GULLS".
findings.actual: Pause phases differ from season to season. F146 gap starts in the scored curves (and in the epoch table): season 0 = 0.99, 2.49, 21.49, 31.48, 35.24, 62.24, 69.49 d (the mask in pipeline/train.py RMDC26_GAPS_D); season 1 = 0.99 (12.1 h), 24.24, 35.24, 42.74, 66.0, 69.49; season 2 = 0.99 (12.1 h), 16.99, 33.74, 35.24, 50.74, 69.49; season 7 = 0.99, 8.74, 25.24, 35.24, 42.74, 49.99, 69.49; season 8 = 0.99 (12.1 h), 6.75, 35.24, 41.24, 43.99, 69.49; season 9 = 0.99, 3.24, 7.99, 35.24, 41.99, 49.73, 69.49. Only 3 of the 7 phases recur, and three of six seasons have six pauses, one of them ~12 h. The 'exact' mask therefore matches only season 0, which holds 9,172 of the 56,975 scored events (16.1%). By season, the exact-schedule arm (ft_sched_norelabel) flags 12.5% of season-0 single lenses and 42.3% in the other five seasons (random-gap arm: 11.8% and 11.8%), which accounts for its 37.4% overall FA. Within season 0 (5,561 1S1L, 1,734 1S2L) it beats random gaps at matched budgets: 0.213 vs 0.145 at 2%, 0.300 vs 0.237 at 5.2% (difference +0.063, bootstrap 95% [0.044, 0.089]), 0.450 vs 0.405 at 11.7%. The reported null transfer result is an artifact of a mask that is wrong for 84% of the test set. Table gap, the 0.949 calibration (calibrate_gapped_threshold.py gap_mask_f146) and the sched arms all use the season-0 pattern.
findings.how_checked: Epoch-table segmentation (gaps > 5 d, then in-season diffs > 1 h). F146 times from one 5.6 MB curve-cache chunk, one event per season. Per-season FA and matched-budget recall from rows_full_sched_{rand,sched_norelabel}.json with t0 mapped to season. 500-sample bootstrap.
findings.fix: Describe the schedule as season-dependent. Rerun the exact-schedule arm with per-season masks (or score it per season) before drawing any transfer conclusion. Revise ledger row 2 and the 'does not transfer better' sentence, and re-derive the gapped calibration.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced. From the epoch table, the pause phases per season are: s0 0.99/2.49/21.49/31.48/35.24/62.24/69.49 d; s1 0.99(12.1h)/24.24/35.24/42.74/66.0/69.49; s2, s7, s8, s9 all differ. Per-event F146 times in c_306427_307083_250.npz match, one event per season. train.py RMDC26_GAPS_D equals season 0 only, which holds 9,172/56,975 events. Frozen-threshold FA by season: norelabel 0.125/0.378/0.451/0.361/0.359/0.561 vs rand 0.118/0.113/0.107/0.128/0.138/0.104. In season 0, 1S2L recall at the 5.2% budget is 0.302 vs 0.238 (bootstrap diff +0.068 [0.045, 0.091]); in the other seasons it is 0.263 vs 0.281. 'Artifact' overstates it slightly: the null result is confounded, and a gain is shown for season 0 only. calibrate_gapped_threshold.gap_mask_f146 also uses the season-0 phases.

findings.claim: "the planetary population is harder than ours at matched amplitude: the median q is a factor of several below our prior's, and the amplitude selection below keeps faint perturbations"; "RMDC26's planetary population is harder than our prior's"
findings.actual: GULLS median Planet_q: scored 1S2L 1.43e-4, scored 2S2L 1.19e-4 (whole classes 1.42e-4 / 1.24e-4). Against the generator prior (priors.py LogU(1e-6,1); prior-weighted median in the work15 pool 9.9e-4), GULLS is 7.0x / 8.4x lower. Against the planetary part of that prior (q<1e-2, median 1.0e-4), GULLS is 1.2-1.4x HIGHER. Against the class the in-distribution completeness is measured on (paper/results test set, NonPSPL-labelled, n=42,805: median q 0.131, 82% with q>1e-2), GULLS is about 900-1,100x lower. Against our detectable planetary binaries (q<1e-2, median 2.3e-3), GULLS detectable planets (median 1.51e-4 / 1.23e-4) are 15-19x lower. At matched metadata amplitude (>=0.1 mag), GULLS planets are far MORE often detectable under our own label policy: 55.9% / 53.7% versus 5.3% for our prior-weighted binaries with q<0.03, and 13.1% for all our binaries. By amplitude bin 0.3-1 mag: 53% vs 4.9%. By q bin 1e-4 to 1e-3: 58% vs 3.4%. Reweighted to GULLS cells in q+amp+s+|u0|: 54.5% vs 18.7%; adding m_base: 57.5% vs 18.1%. Only the DETECTABLE anomalies are weaker in GULLS: median dchi2_anomaly 3,185 / 5,385 versus 34,040 for the paper test NonPSPL class (10,680 for its q<0.03 part). The population is therefore not 'harder at matched amplitude'. The in-distribution comparison fails because our anomaly class is 82% stellar-mass-ratio binaries, and RMDC26 has none (max q 0.03).
findings.how_checked: Planet_q came from the metadata joined to the scored rows. Our prior was checked in cadence_local_work/work15/mm_train and fspl5s_local_work/mm_train params.npy, weighted by 1/keep_prob (BYPRODUCT_KEEP 0.15 undone), and in paper/results params.npy, label.npy, test_idx.npy and dchi2_anomaly.npy. For GULLS detectability I used gulls_truth_cache label_detect (6,600 events, which reproduce the fractions in transfer_detectability_relabel.json). For our detectability I used label==NonPSPL. Amplitude was the same single-lens formula on u0 and f_s_F146. Scripts: harder.py, harder2.py, ours3.py. Caveat: this assumes detectability_relabel.py and assemble apply the same rule, which is the project's own claim.
findings.fix: Replace with: 'RMDC26's anomalous classes are entirely planetary (q<=0.03, median 1.2-1.4e-4), whereas 82% of our NonPSPL evaluation events are stellar-mass-ratio binaries (median q 0.13). GULLS' detectable anomalies are correspondingly weaker (median Delta-chi2 about 4e3 vs 3e4).' Drop 'harder at matched amplitude' and 'a factor of several below our prior'. findings.verdict_note: The evidence checks out. Paper test NonPSPL: n 42,805, median q 0.131, 82.2% q>1e-2, median Δχ²_anom 34,037. work15 amp>=0.1 binaries are policy-detectable 13.1% (weighted), 5.2% for q<0.03, against GULLS 55.9/53.7%. findings.claim: 'the schedule itself, not the model, hides about half of these planets, whose anomaly sits in the unobserved gap'; [D] 'the planets lost are lost to the 110-day gaps rather than to the model'; row 9 'the lost half of the planets is lost to the schedule, not the model'.
findings.actual: The data do not support 'about half'. A claimable anomaly is visible in the wings for 51.7% (475/919) of scorable 1S2L and 43.75% (385/880) of 2S2L. In-season the figures are 55.9% (1398/2500) and 53.7% (1342/2500), so the schedule costs 4.2 and 9.9 points (8.4 and 15.2 if unscorable events count). The other ~half have no claimable anomaly anywhere, as in-season. (1) Caustic timing: the predicted planetary-caustic time t0 ± tE·sqrt((s−1/s)²−u0²) falls inside a dense season for 95.1% / 83.6% of the scorable peak-in-gap planets. Those events are wing-detectable at 53.7% / 48.2%; the in-season analogue is 56.7% / 55.2%. (2) The population is selected by GULLS: every 1S2L/2S2L in the release has ObsGroup_0_chi2 ≥ 60 (none of 35,647 / 42,886 below; 0.29% of 1S1L are). That column rank-correlates 0.81 / 0.80 with our dchi2_anomaly but only 0.21 with dchi2_event. Peak-in-gap events make up 10.4% / 11.8% of eligible binaries against 31.3% of 1S1L. Only 2.7% / 6.0% of the peak-in-gap planets are near-resonant (0.8 < s < 1.25), against 54% / 53% in-season; median caustic offset is 50 / 53 d against 3.6 / 4.9 d. So planets whose anomaly fell in a gap are largely absent from RMDC26, and this sample cannot measure how many the schedule hides. (3) Model: at the frozen threshold the combiner catches 0.276 / 0.325 of wing-detectable anomalies, against 0.474 / 0.557 in-season, so more planets are lost to the model than to the schedule. In 80% of the scored wing seasons t0 is more than 0.5 tE outside the window, beyond the training t0 padding (t0_pad_tE = 0.5).

findings.actual: Off-by-one on both ends. k0 = ceil((tc-step)/res)+1 skips the first fine point after the previous coarse cut, and arange(k0, floor(tc/res)) drops the last point before tc. The fine scan never tests 7.0, 7.5, 14.0, 14.5, 21.5, 22.0, 28.5, 29.0, 43.0, 43.5, 50.0, 50.5, 57.5, 58.0, 64.5 or 65.0 d. On those 1,000 seeds the HEAD default equals the cascade's first-detectable onset (committed t_anom_fine) for only 826. Of the rest, 68 are off the 0.5-d grid (coarse 7.2k values), 149 are later (43 by 7 d or more, max 56 d) and 25 are earlier. The off-by-one alone changes 82/1000. In the actual fspl5s_v2 training pool, 0 of 14,756 onsets fall on the 16 skipped points, while 1,249 (8.5%) carry off-grid coarse values. 126 of these sit at 21.6 d, inside the 21.49 d pause, so the fixed-schedule relabel still fires spuriously for 0.85% of binaries. Finally, the anomaly statistic is an F146 PSPL refit, which cannot separate a planetary deviation from a binary-source one. With three bands the flag rate is 45% at <5 mmag, 39% at 5-10, 38% at 10-20 and 39% at 20-50 mmag (flat), rising only above 0.1 mag. With F146-only input it becomes monotone and much lower: 16%, 21%, 28%, 43%, 72%. The high sub-floor flag rate therefore comes from the colour bands, not from the anomaly the policy measures.

gaps: GULLS was used for design and model selection, and no verifier assessed this. The sidecar was picked from at least 7 checkpoints on the same 56,975 events (REVISION row 8: 'better on the external test'). The single-lens rho prior was widened 'to cover GULLS' single-lens rho' from GULLS metadata. bkg_mult was fitted to GULLS noise. The amplitude and tE cuts were designed after the first run 'returned PeriodicVar almost uniformly' (gulls_transfer.py comments). The fspl5s numbers are therefore best-of-N on the test set. The draft's 'We use it as a test set … no threshold was chosen on it' and 'trained only on our own simulations' need qualifying.

Training-seed variance was never used to judge between-checkpoint claims; every arm is single-seed. The closest replicate pair (rand vs g08e12, same recipe, different pools) differs by 0.014/0.020/0.023 at the 2/5.2/11.7% budgets. That is the size of the v2-vs-v1 gap (0.015), fspl5s-vs-fspl (0.021) and norelabel-vs-rand (0.013), which the text interprets as real effects ('marginally worse', 'slightly hurt', 'matches').

The cascade comparison mixes models. The in-house cascade (1.6%, +5.0 d, 89%) is from the shipped checkpoint (cascade_reproduce_result.json model 'shipped (cascade-trained)') on 80% stellar-q binaries, while the GULLS cascade uses fspl5s. 'The timing behaviour transfers' compares different models, and no in-house fspl5s cascade was run.

The 0.949 calibration's gapped arm (calibrate_gapped_threshold.gap_mask_f146, called with mask=None at l.101) blanks only the seven season-0 pauses.
